absent: Numeric values and full state diagram for idle, kicked, and flushing optimizer states, the optimize delay duration, and the pass counter width.

Bodies and contracts for unlisted helpers such as pending revert collection, pending optimize application, optimized lookup at an address, readiness and disabled and unused and queued and aggregated and gone and ftrace predicates, and instance management.

Architecture specific probe operations including optimized check, optimized preparation, prepared bytes test, optimized removal, unoptimization, arm, disarm, slot preparation, ftrace slot preparation, and plain removal.
Data layouts and constant values for the optimized container, base probe, instruction slot, queue and hash linkage, table size, hit status, and flag bits for optimized, disabled, gone, and disarmed.

Synchronization and reclamation primitives including task quiescence wait, RCU grace wait, variable wait and wake on the pass counter, CPU read lock and jump label lock and text mutex internals, and RCU list traversal and mutation.
Ftrace integration details including filter management, function registration lifetime, handler behavior, and the effect of permanent disable beyond teardown short circuit.
Sysctl framework behavior including hierarchy registration, bounded integer parsing, permission enforcement, and the exact user visible messages for enable and disable.

findings.text: A dedicated optimizer thread sleeps interruptibly until shared state leaves idle or a stop arrives. On a normal kick it waits a bounded delay that a flush request or stop can interrupt, then it marks state idle and runs one complete optimizer pass before sleeping again.

Each optimizer pass takes the main kprobe lock plus CPU read protection plus text protection, reverts queued probes and collects unused disarmed ones, waits for tasks quiescence so preempted CPUs leave rewritten ranges, then applies pending optimizations and releases cleaned aggregators. After dropping those guards it advances a pass counter, wakes flush waiters, and re-kicks itself when either queue remains non empty.

Shared optimizer state moves among idle and kicked and flushing. A kick succeeds only from idle and wakes the thread. A flusher exchanges the state to flushing and wakes the thread when the previous value differed. The thread resets the value to idle immediately before each pass.

Optimization is attempted only for probes reported ready when global optimization is allowed and neither the probe nor the global disarm state disables it, and only when no post handler is present and an architecture check accepts the site. An already optimized probe that sits on the revert queue is simply dequeued, otherwise the optimized mark is set and the entry is placed on the pending optimize queue followed by a kick. Entries on pending optimize or revert queues must carry the optimized mark and must have been link empty before queuing.

Revert handling distinguishes queued and active probes. A probe already on the revert queue stays there unless forced, in which case the architecture revert runs immediately with clearing of the optimized mark and the entry moves to the freeing queue. A probe on the optimize queue is dequeued and its optimized mark cleared. An active optimized probe is either reverted immediately when forced or placed on the revert queue with a kick.

Cleaning walks the freeing queue safely, detaches each entry, warns once when the entry is unexpectedly still in use and leaves that case in place, otherwise looks up another probe at the same address and retries its optimization before releasing the aggregator.

The main kprobe mutex serializes kicks, flush waits, global enable and disable scans, and the whole optimizer pass. Flush waiters loop while either pending queue is non empty, record the pass counter, request flushing state with a wakeup, then sleep on the counter while temporarily dropping the mutex, so an observed increment proves a full pass completed.

Code patching paths require CPU read protection together with text protection, with an additional jump label guard when preparing optimization or registering an aggregator. Low level arm and disarm helpers assert text protection, and the immediate revert helper asserts CPU protection. Public arm and disarm wrappers acquire CPU read plus text protection around the low level helpers unless the probe uses the ftrace path.

Reuse expects an unused disabled aggregator that is still linked for delayed revert, clears the disabled mark, verifies readiness, and re queues optimization, returning an error when not ready. Termination dequeues any pending queue linkage, clears the optimized mark, moves an unused entry from the revert queue to the freeing queue, and invokes architecture removal without touching patched code. Without optimization support reuse is impossible and warns.

Aggregator allocation creates a zeroed optimized container, initializes its queue linkage, copies the target address, and runs architecture preparation through a helper that skips ftrace based probes. Initialization copies the instruction slot, flushes it, copies address and flags without the optimized mark, installs shared pre dispatch and conditional post dispatch, initializes list and hash linkage, then links the new member with RCU semantics and replaces the hash node.

When jump optimization is not configured, optimization and revert and termination and preparation and global try operations become inert, low level arm and disarm map directly to architecture arm and disarm, allocation returns a plain zeroed probe, and the flush wait collapses to only a lock assertion with no thread initialization.
A public blocking helper acquires the main kprobe guard and then waits until both the pending optimize queue and the pending revert queue drain, allowing callers to flush all delayed code patching.

Blacklist checking first consults an architecture predicate covering the protected kprobes text range, then scans an RCU protected interval list under RCU protection, and finally resolves suffixed symbols by truncating at the dot and rechecking the base address, treating any interval hit as prohibited.

Shared pre dispatch walks the member list under RCU, skips disabled members without a handler, installs each eligible member as the current instance around its handler call, clears the instance afterwards, and stops with success when any pre handler reports success. Shared post dispatch similarly invokes every eligible post handler with the supplied flags while maintaining the current instance.

Miss counting increments a lone probe directly but fans out to every member when the probe aggregates others. Busy marking disables preemption, installs a sentinel probe whose address is the lookup routine and whose status is active, and later clears the current probe and reenables preemption.

Registration under CPU read plus jump label plus text protection creates an aggregator when the existing probe is not aggregated, rescues a dying aggregator when it is unused, reallocates an instruction slot and re prepares optimization when the aggregator was marked gone while keeping it disabled, copies the slot to the newcomer, and links the newcomer. When the aggregator was disabled but the newcomer is enabled, it enables and arms the aggregator unless globally disarmed, and on arm failure it restores disabled state, detaches the newcomer, and waits for RCU grace.

Membership of a post handler forces fallback to an unoptimized breakpoint and causes installation of shared post dispatch when absent. The optimizer refuses any probe carrying a post handler, and the global try path refuses ftrace based probes before allocating an aggregator.

Ftrace backed probes use two operation sets selected by presence of a post handler, with separate usage counts for plain and address modifying cases. Count zero triggers function registration after filter installation, with filter rollback on registration failure. Teardown unregisters at last user, decrements the count, and removes the filter while warning on errors. A permanent disable flag makes teardown report success without action.

Preparation chooses an ftrace specific architecture path for ftrace based probes and the normal architecture path otherwise. Public arm and disarm take the ftrace path directly when applicable, otherwise they hold CPU read plus text protection around low level patching. Low level arm forces revert of any overlapping optimized occupant before patching and then tries optimization, while low level disarm attempts revert first and touches architecture state only when the probe is not left queued, optionally retrying an overlapped sibling.

Rewriting several bytes as a jump risks a preempted task resuming inside the new jump, so the optimizer waits for tasks quiescence between revert and optimize phases. Overlapping optimized sites are also hazardous: arming a new probe forces revert of any optimized occupant, and disarming or freeing retries optimization of a blocked sibling.

The user toggle handler serializes concurrent writes with a dedicated sysctl mutex, refreshes the visible integer from the current global allow state, delegates integer parsing to the generic bounded vector handler, then enables or disables optimization globally according to the resulting value.
Global jump optimization is controlled by debug leaf kprobes-optimization holding zero or one with mode 0644, initialized at boot.

An optimized probe container embeds a base probe plus intrusive queue linkage plus an optimized instruction buffer. Callers recover the container from a base probe pointer through standard container linkage.
Early initialization creates the optimizer wait queue, marks shared state idle, and starts the optimizer kernel thread.
A public predicate reports whether a given optimized container currently sits on the pending revert queue by linear search.
A public preparation helper forwards to architecture preparation for ordinary probes while doing nothing for ftrace based probes.

Public services increment missed counts with aggregator fan out, bracket busy regions that install a sentinel current probe under disabled preemption, and permanently disable the ftrace acceleration path.
Without ftrace support both ftrace arm and disarm report device not available.
Two ftrace operation objects share a common handler, one requesting register preservation and the other additionally requesting address modification permission, with separate usage counts.
The non optimized aggregator release path removes architecture state for the probe and then frees its storage.

Enabling scans the whole hash table under the main lock with CPU read protection, sets the global allow flag once, and queues every enabled probe for optimization. Disabling clears the flag, queues every enabled probe for revert, releases CPU protection, then blocks until both queues drain.

The global try path for an ordinary probe takes CPU read plus jump label plus text protection, allocates an aggregator, verifies that optimized bytes were prepared and otherwise removes architecture state and frees the attempt, then initializes aggregation and kicks the optimizer without patching synchronously.
